title: Negative correlation in uniform forests
statement: For every finite simple graph, does its uniform acyclic edge subset have pairwise nonpositive edge covariance?

status_search.scope: March 2026 primary paper still states general conjecture; later complete-graph results do not settle arbitrary graphs

title: Self-avoiding-walk counting exponents
statement: Determine the asymptotic correction to c_n=mu^n for lattice self-avoiding walks in dimensions two, three, and four.
statement_caveat: The source predicts gamma_2=43/32 and explicitly requires logarithmic corrections in dimension four. High-dimensional cases already proved are excluded from the unresolved target. This remains one source problem, not separate parameter rows.

title: Hexagonal self-avoiding-walk scaling limit
statement: Does the rescaled uniform n-step hexagonal-lattice self-avoiding walk converge to SLE_(8/3)?
statement_caveat: The source leaves the precise rescaling, curve topology, parametrization and limiting SLE geometry implicit; these are proof obligations, not permissions to change the question.

title: Existence of the quenched connective limit
statement: On the infinite supercritical bond-percolation cluster of Z^2, does c_n(v)^(1/n) converge almost surely, independently of v?
status_search_lead: Lacoin arXiv:1203.6051 establishes a deterministic limsup and strict annealed comparison; a limsup theorem alone does not answer the limit question.

title: Ehrenfest mirror escape
statement: Which mirror densities p give positive escape probability in the square-lattice model with equally likely NE/NW mirrors?

title: Poisson mirror escape threshold
statement: For nondegenerate Poisson-mirror orientation laws, characterize escape below the vacant-set threshold, including uniform orientations.
statement_caveat: All three source subquestions are grouped to avoid counting nested parameter variants separately. The direction quantifier for theta_mu must be resolved from the model before a theorem claim.

title: Unbounded mirror component trapping every ray
statement: Can an unbounded component of a mirror complement contain an origin from which every reflected ray stays bounded?

title: Diffusive Poisson mirror trajectories
statement: For rationally supported nondegenerate mirror orientations, do escaping trajectories have finite positive diffusivity and a Gaussian limit?

title: Manhattan pinball localization
statement: Does every positive mirror density localize the Manhattan-oriented pinball trajectory?

title: Biased random square-lattice orientations
statement: Does every nonzero orientation bias give positive probability of an infinite directed path from the origin?

title: Brownian SIR survival in dimensions at least two
statement: Does the fully diffusing Poisson Brownian SIR model survive for sufficiently small positive removal rate when d>=2?

title: Complete bunkbed inequality
resolution_scope: Complete BBC with all horizontal and vertical edges independently retained at p=1/2. Theorem 1.2 concerns a fixed transversal set, so it is not by itself an exact match.

title: One-dimensional Brownian snails extinction
resolution_locator: Hartarsky-Lichev, Theorem 1.1, PDF page 3, ECP 28 (2023), article 45
resolution_scope: For any positive Poisson intensity and removal rate in dimension one, extinction time has an exponential tail for sufficiently large time.

statement: For symmetric order-r tensors T_i on R^d, p>=2 and independent standard Gaussians g_i, is E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) bounded by polylog(d,n) times O_(r,p)(d^(1/2-1/p) sqrt(sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2))?
statement_caveat: The unresolved range is p<2r apart from known matrix and other special cases. The source says p>=2r is proved. All parameters remain one problem.
title: Gaussian tensor type-2 bound

statement: For G distributed as G(n,1/2), is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?
statement_caveat: Theta is the SDP with PSD matrix, trace one, and zero entries on graph edges.
title: Expected Lovasz theta of a dense independent-edge graph

statement: For the graph on Z/nZ formed by independently including each unordered nonzero generator pair {k,-k} with probability 1/2, is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?
statement_caveat: The inverse-pair convention includes the order-two generator once when n is even; this differs substantively from independent edges.
title: Expected Lovasz theta of a random circulant graph

statement: Let p_M be the probability that a complex Gaussian (4M-5)-by-M matrix gives an injective phaseless measurement map modulo global phase. Is p_M<1 for each meaningful M, and does p_M tend to zero?
statement_caveat: M>=2 is needed for the matrix size to be meaningful. The two clauses are retained as one source conjecture, not counted twice.
title: Random complex phase-retrieval injectivity at 4M-5 measurements

statement: For a (2M-1)-by-M matrix of independent standard real Gaussians, determine the asymptotic size of omega(A), the minimum smallest singular value over row subsets whose complement has rank below M. In particular determine whether its decay is exponential and identify the exponential rate.
statement_caveat: Almost surely every M-row subset is nonsingular, so the minimum reduces to M-row subsets. Interpret asymptotic size in probability; the source does not specify a convergence mode or a normalized logarithmic limit.
title: Worst square-submatrix conditioning in a Gaussian frame

statement: Is there a universal positive lower bound for the Euclidean Cheeger constant of every isotropic log-concave probability measure, in every dimension?
statement_caveat: Use outer boundary liminf in the standard definition; the source's displayed halfspace formula has an S/H notational mismatch. Thin-shell and slicing results are separate and reported resolved by this source.
title: Dimension-free log-concave Poincare or Cheeger constant

statement: For each fixed graph shape alpha with specified left and right index sets, form M_alpha by summing injective labelings with products of independent Rademacher edge variables. Must E||M_alpha|| be Theta(n^f(alpha) (log n)^g(alpha)) for some shape-dependent exponents?
statement_caveat: The target is the general existence of sharp exponents, not a separate problem for every shape. Definitions of overlapping or internal vertex sets must follow the full cited graph-matrix convention.
title: Sharp polynomial-logarithmic expected norm of graph matrices

statement: For Brownian motion exiting a domain in dimension d>2, is the set of limiting approach directions at the exit point almost surely a sphere or a hemisphere?
statement_caveat: The question is meaningful on finite exit; either condition on finite exit or restrict to bounded domains. Do not call infinite exit a counterexample to the intended geometric question.
title: Brownian exit approach directions in higher dimensions

statement: Almost surely, can every two points outside the trace of planar Brownian motion on [0,1] be connected by a Jordan arc meeting the trace at only finitely many points?
statement_caveat: The quantifier is simultaneous over all pairs of outside points, not a single deterministic pair.
title: Finite-crossing arcs through a planar Brownian trace

statement: Delete from a planar Brownian trace on [0,1] all boundaries of connected components of its complement. Is the remaining set totally disconnected almost surely?
statement_caveat: This is a different topological property from Problem 2(i), although a negative answer is stated to imply a negative answer there.
title: Interior remainder of planar Brownian trace

statement: Is the infimum of Hausdorff dimensions of nontrivial Jordan arcs contained in a planar Brownian trace on [0,1] equal to one almost surely?
statement_caveat: A nontrivial arc contains at least two distinct points. The lower bound one alone is not a solution.
title: Percolation dimension of a planar Brownian trace

statement: In any acute triangle, can reflected Brownian motions from distinct starting points be coupled so their meeting-time tail decays at every exponential rate strictly below the first positive Neumann spectral rate?
statement_caveat: Check the generator convention in Burdzy-Kendall (2000): the page calls its rate a Laplacian eigenvalue. A factor-two convention discrepancy is not a solution of the coupling question.
title: Efficient reflected-Brownian coupling in acute triangles

statement: Does some bounded connected smooth planar domain admit synchronously coupled reflected Brownian motions whose distance has positive limsup with positive probability?
statement_caveat: The page states that any such domain must have at least two holes by existing results.
title: Failure of synchronous contraction in a bounded planar domain

statement: For synchronously coupled reflected Brownian motions in the exterior of a nondegenerate closed disk, can their distance have positive limsup with positive probability?
statement_caveat: This unbounded exterior geometry differs from the bounded-domain existence question.
title: Synchronous reflection outside a disk

statement: For N>=3 Brownian particles in any bounded open connected domain, killed at the boundary and immediately cloned from a uniformly selected survivor, are the successive death times almost surely non-accumulating?
statement_caveat: N=2 is explicitly reported solved by Kwasnicki (2024). The earlier general proof had an irreparable error; it is not admissible evidence for the general result.
title: Non-explosion of Fleming-Viot Brownian particles in arbitrary domains

statement: If reflected Brownian motions in a bounded connected domain can remain a positive distance apart forever with positive probability, must there be such a coupling with one path a fixed deterministic function of the other at each time?
statement_caveat: Regularity sufficient to define the intended reflected Brownian motion needs to be fixed from the cited background. A metric-graph counterexample on the page is not a Euclidean-domain counterexample.
title: Rigidity of shy reflected-Brownian couplings

statement: Concatenate independent Brownian path segments cut at stopping times indexed by all integers, with lengths uniformly bounded by a deterministic constant and divergent sums in both directions. Is the resulting path two-sided Brownian after some random time shift?
statement_caveat: The paper's related backward-Brownian question and its almost-sure random bound are recorded as related variants, not an extra count. Independent lengths alone are not the same as stopping times depending on their Brownian paths.
title: Bounded independent Brownian pieces and two-sided Brownian motion

statement: Uniformly label an n-by-n square grid and condition on exactly two local maxima. Does their graph distance divided by n converge in distribution to zero?
statement_caveat: This is the literal displayed question, despite the heading about repulsion. Verify against Twin peaks (2020) before correcting the sign or reporting a counterexample.
title: Separation of two peaks in random square-grid labelings

statement: Does a decomposable forward Brownian motion which is also backward Brownian necessarily become two-sided Brownian after a random shift? The source also asks weaker related formulations using independence of past and future at a random time.
statement_caveat: The three linked formulations are grouped as one compatibility problem. A general process that is both forward and backward Brownian without the extra assumptions is already counterexampled in the paper.
title: Compatibility of forward and backward Brownian decompositions

statement: In a two-sided independent concatenation, use unit-length Brownian segments except at increasingly rare negative-time indices where segments stop on first hitting -1. Characterize frequencies giving backward or two-sided Brownian motion.
statement_caveat: The exact deterministic or random schedule is part of the classification; do not invent a schedule and count it as another sourced question.
title: Sparse first-passage pieces in a forward Brownian concatenation

statement: Given a process whose law on nonnegative time is equivalent to Wiener measure, can a random finite prefix be added, on an enlarged probability space if necessary, to produce a process with Wiener law?
statement_caveat: No independence or Brownian stopping-time restriction is explicit in the source. The candidate proof uses a finite nonnegative integer random time depending on entire paths and auxiliary randomness.
title: Embedding an equivalent Brownian law by adding a finite prefix

statement: On the infinite supercritical bond-percolation cluster of Z^2, does c_n(v)^(1/n) converge almost surely, independently of v?
status_search_lead: Lacoin arXiv:1203.6051 establishes a deterministic limsup and strict annealed comparison; a limsup theorem alone does not answer the limit question.
title: Existence of the quenched connective limit

statement: If a consistent equivariant Borel flow rule has a stationary probability measure equivalent to Galton-Watson law, must the associated subtree Markov chain be ergodic?
statement_caveat: The definition permits zero child weights. Strict positivity is a separate sufficient hypothesis in Proposition 17.17. Exercise 17.22 only treats a merely absolutely continuous stationary measure.
title: Ergodicity of stationary Galton-Watson flows

statement: Start at the origin in Z^2; after first visiting a site step horizontally with either sign equally likely, and after a repeat visit step vertically with either sign equally likely. Does any site receive infinitely many visits with positive probability?
statement_caveat: The source indexing omits the first step; use its intended new-site rule also at time zero. The analogous four- and three-dimensional results do not decide this planar model.
title: Recurrence of the planar horizontal-new vertical-old walk

statement: For a Cayley graph of exponential growth rate b and 1<lambda<b, does the distance from the identity divided by time for RW_lambda converge almost surely to a strictly positive speed?
statement_caveat: RW_lambda uses the source's radial conductances, favoring motion toward the identity for lambda>1. The case lambda=1 may have zero speed and is excluded.
title: Positive speed of inward-biased walks below the Cayley growth rate

statement: If T is any geodesic spanning tree rooted at the identity of a Cayley graph of growth rate b, must br(T)=b, equivalently must its Bernoulli bond percolation threshold be 1/b?
statement_caveat: The branching-number/percolation equivalence is a theorem of the source. The question is stated there geometrically; its probability formulation is recorded transparently. Lexicographically minimal spanning trees satisfy it.
title: Percolation threshold on arbitrary geodesic Cayley spanning trees

statement: For increasing events A,B on edge subsets, is the probability of their disjoint occurrence under any weighted uniform spanning-tree law at most P(A)P(B)?
statement_caveat: Disjoint witnesses use disjoint edge-coordinate sets. Arbitrary events are excluded; negative association for fixed disjoint coordinates is weaker. Goldman 2023 proves a special class generated by simple points.
title: BK disjoint occurrence for weighted uniform spanning trees

statement: Is every infinite Bernoulli percolation cluster on a transient Cayley graph almost surely transient?
statement_caveat: The claim concerns all infinite clusters simultaneously. Nonamenable and Euclidean cases have substantial existing results.
title: Transience preserved in Cayley percolation clusters

statement: Does simple random walk on a Cayley graph have positive speed if and only if simple random walk on its infinite Bernoulli percolation clusters has positive speed almost surely?
statement_caveat: Use graph distance in the cluster for the cluster speed as in the source context; compare with ambient speed carefully. Nonamenable cases are reported known.
title: Positive-speed equivalence for Cayley percolation clusters

statement: Does every locally finite quasi-transitive graph with exactly one end have Bernoulli percolation uniqueness threshold p_u<1?
statement_caveat: A one-ended finite-presentation class is known. The assertion p_c<1 alone is weaker and now resolved in the transitive setting.
title: Uniqueness threshold below one in one-ended transitive graphs

statement: Must p_c(G)<p_u(G) for every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph? The source's related formulation asks whether the property p_c<p_u is preserved by rough isometries among quasi-transitive graphs.
statement_caveat: The closely linked rough-isometry conjecture is grouped here to avoid counting a reformulation separately. Nonunimodular and many other cases are established.
title: Nonuniqueness phase for nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs

statement: Is a finitely generated group amenable exactly when every Cayley graph from every finite generating set has bootstrap complete-occupation critical probability p(G,k) in {0,1} for every threshold k?
statement_caveat: Initially each vertex is occupied independently with probability p; vacant vertices with at least k occupied neighbors become occupied. Criticality is for positive probability of eventual occupation of all vertices.
title: Bootstrap thresholds as a characterization of amenable groups

statement: If G is quasi-transitive and p_c(G)<1, is there almost surely no infinite Bernoulli cluster at p_c(G)?
statement_caveat: Do not count each lattice dimension as a separate problem. Known nonamenable and high-dimensional cases do not settle the entire assertion.
title: Absence of infinite clusters at critical percolation

statement: For an infinite network, is there a coupling (W,F) of its wired and free uniform spanning forests with W subset F almost surely whose joint law is invariant under all network automorphisms?
statement_caveat: Strassen gives an unconstrained monotone coupling. Sofic Cayley groups admit invariant couplings by Lyons-Thom 2016; arbitrary invariant percolations can fail this property.
title: Invariant monotone coupling of free and wired uniform spanning forests

statement: For a Cayley graph of a finitely presented group, is the expected degree at the identity in its free uniform spanning forest rational?
statement_caveat: This is the first l2-Betti-number question via E degree=2+2 beta_1. Counterexamples to broader Atiyah statements must be checked for both first degree and finite presentation before exclusion.
title: Rational expected free-forest degree for finitely presented groups

statement: For any Cayley graph, its free uniform spanning forest F, and epsilon>0, is there an invariant connected random spanning subgraph omega containing F with P(e in omega minus F)<epsilon for every edge e?
statement_caveat: Added edges may depend on F. Independent Bernoulli sprinkling is explicitly known to fail for some nonamenable graphs.
title: Connecting a free uniform spanning forest by arbitrarily sparse invariant additions

statement: On every infinite connected locally finite network, is the number of free uniform spanning-forest components almost surely a constant?
statement_caveat: Automorphisms with an infinite orbit give a positive answer. The remaining arbitrary-network setting lacks that ergodic shortcut.
title: Deterministic component count of the free uniform spanning forest

statement: On every transitive network, is the free uniform spanning forest almost surely connected or composed of infinitely many components?
statement_caveat: The unimodular case was solved by Hutchcroft-Nachmias 2017 and Timar 2018. The unresolved scope retained here is nonunimodular.
title: One or infinitely many free-forest components without unimodularity

statement: On a transitive network with distinct free and wired uniform spanning-forest laws, must every free-forest component have infinitely many ends almost surely?
statement_caveat: The source's subsequent indistinguishability theorem settles the unimodular case. Haar-light components alone do not automatically refute an ends statement.
title: Infinitely many ends in all free-forest components without unimodularity

statement: If the wired and free uniform spanning-forest measures differ on an infinite network, must they be mutually singular?
statement_caveat: Known for trees and networks with an infinite automorphism orbit. Distinct probability measures need not be singular in general.
title: Singularity of distinct free and wired forest measures

statement: For both free and wired uniform spanning forests of an arbitrary infinite network, is the event that every component has one end of probability zero or one?
statement_caveat: Both boundary conditions are grouped. Changing finitely many forest edges can merge components, so tail measurability needs a proof.
title: Zero-one law for all forest components having one end

statement: Along the unique ray from the identity in its wired uniform spanning-forest component, do the finite bushes at successive ray vertices, translated back to the identity, converge in distribution?
statement_caveat: Restrict to Cayley graphs where the stated unique ray exists. The source records solutions for growth at least five and standard Z^2,Z^3,Z^4; the remaining low-growth Cayley cases must be checked individually before any promotion.
title: Limiting bushes along a wired uniform-forest ray

statement: Does each wired minimal spanning-forest component of a nonunimodular transitive graph have one end almost surely?
statement_caveat: The accompanying request for useful nonhomogeneous sufficient conditions is retained as a related extension, not another count.
title: One-ended wired minimal forests without unimodularity

statement: If a quasi-transitive graph has distinct wired and free minimal spanning-forest laws, does every free minimal-forest component have infinitely many ends almost surely?
statement_caveat: The source and later Timar results establish unimodular cases; retain the genuinely remaining scope. All edges have independent continuous labels.
title: Infinitely many ends in free minimal forests distinct from wired

statement: On a nonamenable quasi-transitive graph with p_u<1, is the free minimal spanning forest connected almost surely exactly when Bernoulli percolation has a unique infinite cluster at p_u?
statement_caveat: The source's stronger bijection between forest components and p_u clusters is grouped as a strengthening. One direction is already proved there.
title: Minimal-forest connectivity and uniqueness at p_u

statement: Must both free and wired minimal spanning forests on a quasi-transitive graph have either one or infinitely many components almost surely?
statement_caveat: Free and wired are grouped. Distinct-law unimodular cases are reported resolved by Timar 2018.
title: One or infinitely many minimal-forest components

statement: For a Cayley graph with p_u<1, is there an implication in either direction between multiple infinite clusters at p_u and the nonexistence of an invariant random spanning tree?
statement_caveat: Each condition implies the free minimal spanning forest is disconnected, but a common consequence does not establish either implication.
title: Uniqueness-critical percolation versus invariant spanning trees

statement: Are the components of both free and wired minimal spanning forests on a unimodular transitive graph indistinguishable by every invariant Borel component property?
statement_caveat: Timar 2018 settles the free case when free and wired differ. The remaining equal-law or wired scope is the target.
title: Indistinguishability of minimal spanning-forest components

statement: For a Cayley graph not roughly isometric to Z, does the sequence of translated bushes along a ray in the identity's wired minimal spanning-forest component converge in distribution?
statement_caveat: Uniqueness of that ray is itself tied to critical percolation. Keep the conditional structural assumptions explicit rather than selecting an unmentioned canonical ray.
title: Limiting bushes along a wired minimal-forest ray

statement: For which dimensions d is the minimal spanning forest on Z^d connected almost surely?
statement_caveat: Competing predictions put a transition near dimension six or eight. These dimension variants form one classification problem.
title: Dimensions with a connected Euclidean minimal spanning forest

statement: Does the minimal spanning tree on epsilon Z^2 have a full distributional scaling limit as epsilon tends to zero, in the embedded-tree topology used for its known subsequential limits?
statement_caveat: The source leaves the exact topology to the cited Aizenman-Burchard-Newman-Wilson framework. A triangular-lattice theorem does not settle square-lattice universality.
title: Full scaling limit of the square-lattice minimal spanning tree

statement: If a connected locally finite graph is roughly isometric to a tree, must its free minimal spanning forest be connected almost surely?
statement_caveat: This concerns minimal forests, not uniform forests; Pete-Timar's uniform-forest counterexample cannot be substituted.
title: Connectivity of minimal forests on graphs roughly isometric to trees

statement: For the middle-thirds Cantor set E, let nu_b be harmonic measure on the source's base-b coding tree T[b](E), pushed to E. Is nu_2 mutually singular with the Cantor-Lebesgue measure nu_3?
statement_caveat: Use the coding-tree construction and boundary map in Section 16.2; distinct harmonic measures or dimensions alone do not prove singularity.
title: Singularity of binary and ternary harmonic codings of the Cantor set

statement: For a nondegenerate supercritical Galton-Watson law of mean m under the chapter's moment assumptions, must every consistent equivariant flow rule different almost surely from UNIF have boundary-measure Hausdorff dimension below log m almost surely?
statement_caveat: The source proves a stationary-measure sufficient condition. Difference on a GW-null set is not an admissible counterexample.
title: Dimension drop for every nonuniform Galton-Watson flow

statement: For a nondegenerate supercritical Galton-Watson tree without leaves and 0<=lambda<m, does harmonic-measure dimension of RW_lambda increase with lambda, and is the increase strict?
statement_caveat: On a deterministic regular tree the dimension is constant, so retain the chapter's nondegeneracy assumptions for strictness. Both monotonic and strict clauses are grouped.
title: Monotonicity of harmonic dimension under inward bias

statement: For Galton-Watson trees with p_0=0, is the speed of RW_lambda nonincreasing as the bias parameter lambda increases?
statement_caveat: The transient range is 0<lambda<m; beyond criticality the speed is zero. Positive-regeneration and large-bias partial results are not the complete monotonicity claim.
title: Monotonicity of biased-walk speed on Galton-Watson trees

statement: Is a uniformly random simple 3-regular graph globally synchronizing with probability tending to one? Global synchronization means that every local minimum of sum_(ij in E)(1-cos(theta_i-theta_j)) is a consensus configuration.
statement_caveat: Use even n. Connectivity is necessary but not sufficient; degree-three deterministic examples do not refute an asymptotic random-graph assertion.
title: Global Kuramoto synchronization of random cubic graphs

statement: For uniform U(1) signal x in C^n with |x_i|=1 and independent Wigner noises, observe Y_k=(lambda/n)x^(k)(x^(k))*+W_k/sqrt(n), k=1,...,L_n. Find a scaling of distinct frequencies L_n for which a polynomial-time algorithm reliably detects signal at some fixed lambda<1.
statement_caveat: The source also names finite groups. For a fixed finite group the number of distinct irreducible frequencies is bounded; a growing group or repeated-observation convention must be specified. The unambiguous U(1) case is the admitted target.
title: Subspectral detection from a growing number of synchronization frequencies

statement: In the same multifrequency U(1) or specified finite-group Gaussian synchronization model, fix L independently of n. For signal strength between its statistical threshold and1, is reliable detection possible in time exp(n^delta) for some delta<1?
statement_caveat: The statistical threshold and group must refer to the fixed model. This is a time-accuracy question distinct from growing the observation model in OpenProblem7.
title: Subexponential detection at fixed synchronization frequencies

statement: For even tensor order r and fixed l>=r/2, index M by l-subsets of [n] and set M_IJ=lambda+Z_(I symmetric_difference J) when that difference has size r, and zero otherwise, with independent standard Gaussian Z_S. Does the normalized spectral-outlier threshold n^(r/4) lambda_critical(r,l) tend to zero as l tends to infinity after n tends to infinity?
statement_caveat: The source suppresses the n-dependence of its threshold notation. Its literal inclusion of r=2 needs a separate check against matrix-PCA limits; no silent restriction to r>=4 is made and no r=2 counterexample is yet claimed.
title: Kikuchi spectral thresholds as the polynomial degree increases

statement: For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Ising model with arbitrary external field, does single-site heat-bath Glauber dynamics mix in polynomial total-variation time for every fixed beta<1, with high probability over the Gaussian disorder?
statement_caveat: Keep SK Hamiltonian normalization consistent. A July2026 primary paper proves results for sufficiently large external fields, and an August2026 preprint claims optimal mixing for beta<1/2 uniformly over fields; neither states the full beta<1 arbitrary-field conclusion.

status_search.finding: Large-field result, not arbitrary-field full regime
Preprint claims beta<1/2 uniform fields; full beta<1 remainder not resolved by its statement

title: Polynomial Glauber mixing throughout the SK high-temperature regime

statement: On a finite graph with nest N and food F, ants take edge-weighted random walks until hitting F. Reinforce either a uniformly chosen shortest N-F path in the visited trace, or the loop erasure of the reversed walk. Are all edges whose weights grow linearly contained in shortest N-F paths of the original graph?
statement_caveat: The two reinforcement algorithms form one conjecture family here. The source proves series-parallel and losange cases, not all graphs.
title: Geodesic selection by reinforced ants

locator: OpenProblems1-2, PDF p.2; underlying Kious-Mailler-Schapira Conjecture1.1
statement: When each ant reinforces every edge it visited at least once, do all edge weights divided by the number of ants converge almost surely to deterministic constants on general finite graphs, and does an appropriate edgewise statement hold on Z^2?
statement_caveat: The finite and Z^2 versions are grouped. The underlying paper excludes multiple edges incident to food; the brief workshop statement omits this load-bearing restriction. Its wording main conjecture is interpreted using the immediately preceding trace-process paragraph.
title: Deterministic limits for trace-reinforced ants

statement: For superlinear preferential attachment with iid positive fitness and attachment f(k,w)=w k^p or k^p+w, determine the growth of the maximum degree and the label attaining it in the regime where the limiting tree is locally finite and has one infinite ray.
statement_caveat: Use a positive initial-degree convention; the displayed one-vertex degree-zero multiplicative formula otherwise has a zero denominator. The source model must be initialized consistently.
title: Maximal degree and its location in the infinite-path fitness regime

statement: Determine the scaling and limiting empirical degree distribution of the superlinear preferential-attachment tree with fitness described in Section3, including the infinite-path regime.
statement_caveat: A degree-count measure and a fitness-degree joint measure are different objects; the admitted target is the empirical degree distribution explicitly named in the source.
title: Empirical degree scaling for superlinear attachment with fitness

statement: In the Section3 fitness model, replace one attachment per new vertex by m>=2 choices and determine how the transition between degree condensation and an infinite-path structure changes.
statement_caveat: Sampling with or without replacement and sequential updating must be fixed; the source proposes a multigraph extension. One family is counted for all m, rather than parameter copies.
title: Multiple-attachment phase transition with superlinear fitness

statement: Let a new positive value be sampled from mu with probability beta, and otherwise copy a previous value with probability proportional to value times multiplicity. With ess sup mu=1 and mu({1})=0, find the fluctuation limit of sum_(i<=n)(X_i-lambda_star), where lambda_star is the Section4 law-of-large-numbers constant.
statement_caveat: The source equation beta integral x/(lambda_star-(1-beta)x) dmu=1 defines lambda_star when possible; otherwise lambda_star=1-beta. A universal square-root normalization is not assumed.
title: Fluctuations of fitness-reinforced sequence sums

locator: OpenProblem10 and displayed conjecture, PDF pp.7-8
statement: When beta integral (1-x)^(-1) dmu<1 and mu(1-x,1) is regularly varying at zero with index alpha>1, determine a_n tending to infinity and c>0 for which n^(-1) sum f(a_n(1-X_i)) converges in probability to c integral_0^infinity f(x)e^(-x)x^alpha dx for compactly supported continuous f.
statement_caveat: Convergence against compactly supported test functions does not by itself identify total condensate mass; mass at zero or infinity must be separately controlled.
title: Boundary profile of the reinforced-sequence condensate

statement: For the same innovation/copying scheme with unbounded positive innovation law mu, determine the superlinear growth rate of S_n=sum_(i<=n) X_i as a function of the tail of mu.
statement_caveat: No single rate can be asserted for every unbounded mu without describing its tail; the question is a distribution-dependent classification.
title: Growth of sums with unbounded reinforcement fitness

statement: For a bounded-degree infinite graph, bounded positive vertex firing rates, and WARM exponent 0<alpha<1, establish convergence of every normalized edge count to the intended unique positive equilibrium.
statement_caveat: The source literally says unique equilibrium while allowing nonnegative coordinates. Boundary equilibria make that literal uniqueness false; the meaningful positive-attractor formulation is recorded explicitly, not silently substituted.
title: Weak reinforcement on infinite WARM networks

statement: For WARM on Z with alpha=1 and all vertex firing rates1, prove that each edge count divided by time converges almost surely to1.
statement_caveat: Keep the stochastic count process distinct from its deterministic equilibrium equation.
title: Critical WARM on the integer line

statement: Improve the known sufficient threshold alpha>2 ensuring that every connected component of a stable finite-graph WARM equilibrium is a tree, allowing arbitrary positive firing rates.
statement_caveat: The source identifies the uniform triangle threshold4/3 as a lower obstruction. A rederivation of it is not a new threshold theorem.
title: Sharp reinforcement threshold for WARM forests

statement: For finite WARM graphs with uniform vertex firing rates, improve the sufficient threshold alpha>25 for every surviving stable component to have diameter at most3.
statement_caveat: This is a geometry question beyond the forest conclusion; all alpha values are grouped as one threshold problem.
title: Sharp reinforcement threshold for WARM whiskers

statement: With bounded-degree graph, firing rates bounded above and bounded away from zero, and alpha>1, prove edgewise convergence of normalized WARM counts and finiteness of every component of surviving edges.
statement_caveat: The lower bound on firing rates is essential in the source: examples with decaying rates on trees have infinitely many infinite components.
title: Finite surviving components in infinite superlinear WARM

statement: Do bounded positive firing rates on Z^d, d>=2, which are not bounded away from zero, and some alpha>1 yield a positive probability of an infinite component of surviving WARM edges? If so, determine uniqueness.
statement_caveat: The existence and uniqueness parts are grouped. Tree examples do not directly embed as bounded-length lattice edges.
title: WARM percolation with vanishing rates on lattices

statement: For nearest-neighbor vertex-reinforced random walk on Z, with transition weights w(1+local_time) and positive w satisfying w(x)=o(x^alpha) for some alpha<1, is the walk recurrent?
statement_caveat: The source states positivity and the growth upper bound, without an explicit monotonicity hypothesis. Any use of monotonicity must be flagged.
title: Recurrence of sublinear vertex-reinforced walk on Z

statement: For Z_(n+1)=(1-r-f)Z_n+r X_(n+1)+f p with E[X_(n+1)|F_n]=Q Z_n, Q=A^T irreducible row-stochastic and X binary coordinatewise, determine nonconvergence and the continuous-time limit when r tends to0 and f is asymptotic to c r^2.
statement_caveat: Assume r,f>0 and r+f<=1. The source permits 0<=p<=1, including extreme vectors; those have a different convergence answer. The displayed conditional mean alone does not specify the cross-coordinate noise covariance.
title: Forced network urn convergence and diffusion scaling

statement: Relate the local weak limit of the Dereich-Morters Bernoulli preferential-attachment model, whose older vertices are chosen independently with probability f(in_degree)/(n-1), to an appropriately matched model with iid Poisson outgoing degree and attachment based on in-degree.
statement_caveat: The matching of the affine rule and Poisson parameter is part of the question. Early probabilities exceeding1 need a consistent initialization or cap.
title: Matching local limits of Bernoulli and Poisson-outdegree attachment

statement: Determine local weak limits of preferential-attachment graphs with fixed outgoing degree m>=2 and nonaffine attachment function f, extending the known tree and affine cases.
statement_caveat: State a nonexplosive/noncondensed class of f before expecting a locally finite limit; the source asks for a theory beyond the affine case, not one arbitrary universal formula.
title: Local limits for nonaffine attachment with multiple edges

statement: Extend the two-state interpretation criterion of Theorem1.7 to finite color sets of size at least3, covering critical and supercritical pivot trees even without positive regularity.
statement_caveat: A deterministic automaton acts on child-color counts. Interpretability is measurability of root color from the uncolored Galton-Watson tree; positive-mass colors and the standing offspring assumptions are retained.
title: Multistate pivot-tree criterion for interpretation

statement: Extend the random-tree interpretation and pivot-process theory to infinite state spaces, so it can handle recursive distributional models beyond finite colors.
statement_caveat: The source asks for an extension framework. Finite-type spectral statements cannot be copied unchanged to a countable type space.
title: Infinite-state tree-automaton interpretation criteria

statement: Extend the interpretation/pivot theory when each vertex has iid auxiliary randomness and its state is a function of its child states and that local randomness.
statement_caveat: Endogeny must be relative to the tree plus all vertex innovations; it is a different sigma-field from the bare uncolored tree.
title: Randomized tree automata and endogeny

statement: For a finite color set of size at least3 and a deterministic child-count automaton under the paper standing offspring assumptions, can the distributional map have infinitely many fixed points?
statement_caveat: The one-child identity example is excluded by the genuine-branching assumption. Empty-color embeddings are not used to manufacture examples.
title: Infinitely many fixed points of a finite-color automaton

statement: Given a finite prescribed configuration of two-state fixed points with rogue/interpretable labels, determine whether a deterministic tree automaton and offspring distribution can realize it, including the monotone-automaton restriction.
statement_caveat: Endpoint and multiplicity constraints are part of realizability. The request is not permission to assign arbitrary labels that contradict the pivot criterion.
title: Prescribing rogue and interpretable automaton fixed points

statement: Find structural conditions on a tree automaton itself that force uniqueness of its distributional fixed point, complementing the source condition on a first-order interpretation.
statement_caveat: The condition must involve the offspring law as appropriate; the same rule can undergo bifurcations when that law changes.
title: Automaton-level conditions for a unique fixed point

locator: Question12, PDF p.33; repeated p.146; manuscript26September2016
statement: For iid nonnegative edge times on Z^2 with F(0)=0, is the axial time constant at least the expected minimum of four independent edge times?
statement_caveat: E_4 is expectation of a minimum, not a fourth moment. The target is the universal survey formulation; the motivating simulation paper reports selected families.
title: Four-edge-minimum lower bound for the FPP time constant

statement: Determine the asymptotic correction to c_n=mu^n for lattice self-avoiding walks in dimensions two, three, and four.
statement_caveat: The source predicts gamma_2=43/32 and explicitly requires logarithmic corrections in dimension four. High-dimensional cases already proved are excluded from the unresolved target. This remains one source problem, not separate parameter rows.
title: Self-avoiding-walk counting exponents

statement: Does the rescaled uniform n-step hexagonal-lattice self-avoiding walk converge to SLE_(8/3)?
statement_caveat: The source leaves the precise rescaling, curve topology, parametrization and limiting SLE geometry implicit; these are proof obligations, not permissions to change the question.
title: Hexagonal self-avoiding-walk scaling limit

statement: Which mirror densities p give positive escape probability in the square-lattice model with equally likely NE/NW mirrors?
title: Ehrenfest mirror escape

statement: For nondegenerate Poisson-mirror orientation laws, characterize escape below the vacant-set threshold, including uniform orientations.
statement_caveat: All three source subquestions are grouped to avoid counting nested parameter variants separately. The direction quantifier for theta_mu must be resolved from the model before a theorem claim.
title: Poisson mirror escape threshold

statement: Can an unbounded component of a mirror complement contain an origin from which every reflected ray stays bounded?
title: Unbounded mirror component trapping every ray

statement: For rationally supported nondegenerate mirror orientations, do escaping trajectories have finite positive diffusivity and a Gaussian limit?
title: Diffusive Poisson mirror trajectories

statement: Does every positive mirror density localize the Manhattan-oriented pinball trajectory?
title: Manhattan pinball localization

statement: Does every nonzero orientation bias give positive probability of an infinite directed path from the origin?
title: Biased random square-lattice orientations

statement: Does the fully diffusing Poisson Brownian SIR model survive for sufficiently small positive removal rate when d>=2?
title: Brownian SIR survival in dimensions at least two

statement: For symmetric order-r tensors T_i on R^d, p>=2 and independent standard Gaussians g_i, is E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) bounded by polylog(d,n) times O_(r,p)(d^(1/2-1/p) sqrt(sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2))?
statement_caveat: The unresolved range is p<2r apart from known matrix and other special cases. The source says p>=2r is proved. All parameters remain one problem.
title: Gaussian tensor type-2 bound

statement: For G distributed as G(n,1/2), is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?
statement_caveat: Theta is the SDP with PSD matrix, trace one, and zero entries on graph edges.
title: Expected Lovasz theta of a dense independent-edge graph

statement: For the graph on Z/nZ formed by independently including each unordered nonzero generator pair {k,-k} with probability 1/2, is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?
statement_caveat: The inverse-pair convention includes the order-two generator once when n is even; this differs substantively from independent edges.
title: Expected Lovasz theta of a random circulant graph

statement: Let p_M be the probability that a complex Gaussian (4M-5)-by-M matrix gives an injective phaseless measurement map modulo global phase. Is p_M<1 for each meaningful M, and does p_M tend to zero?
statement_caveat: M>=2 is needed for the matrix size to be meaningful. The two clauses are retained as one source conjecture, not counted twice.
title: Random complex phase-retrieval injectivity at 4M-5 measurements

statement: For a (2M-1)-by-M matrix of independent standard real Gaussians, determine the asymptotic size of omega(A), the minimum smallest singular value over row subsets whose complement has rank below M. In particular determine whether its decay is exponential and identify the exponential rate.
statement_caveat: Almost surely every M-row subset is nonsingular, so the minimum reduces to M-row subsets. Interpret asymptotic size in probability; the source does not specify a convergence mode or a normalized logarithmic limit.
title: Worst square-submatrix conditioning in a Gaussian frame

statement: Is there a universal positive lower bound for the Euclidean Cheeger constant of every isotropic log-concave probability measure, in every dimension?
statement_caveat: Use outer boundary liminf in the standard definition; the source's displayed halfspace formula has an S/H notational mismatch. Thin-shell and slicing results are separate and reported resolved by this source.
title: Dimension-free log-concave Poincare or Cheeger constant

statement: For each fixed graph shape alpha with specified left and right index sets, form M_alpha by summing injective labelings with products of independent Rademacher edge variables. Must E||M_alpha|| be Theta(n^f(alpha) (log n)^g(alpha)) for some shape-dependent exponents?
statement_caveat: The target is the general existence of sharp exponents, not a separate problem for every shape. Definitions of overlapping or internal vertex sets must follow the full cited graph-matrix convention.
title: Sharp polynomial-logarithmic expected norm of graph matrices

statement: For Brownian motion exiting a domain in dimension d>2, is the set of limiting approach directions at the exit point almost surely a sphere or a hemisphere?
statement_caveat: The question is meaningful on finite exit; either condition on finite exit or restrict to bounded domains. Do not call infinite exit a counterexample to the intended geometric question.
title: Brownian exit approach directions in higher dimensions

statement: Almost surely, can every two points outside the trace of planar Brownian motion on [0,1] be connected by a Jordan arc meeting the trace at only finitely many points?
statement_caveat: The quantifier is simultaneous over all pairs of outside points, not a single deterministic pair.
title: Finite-crossing arcs through a planar Brownian trace

statement: Delete from a planar Brownian trace on [0,1] all boundaries of connected components of its complement. Is the remaining set totally disconnected almost surely?
statement_caveat: This is a different topological property from Problem 2(i), although a negative answer is stated to imply a negative answer there.
title: Interior remainder of planar Brownian trace

statement: Is the infimum of Hausdorff dimensions of nontrivial Jordan arcs contained in a planar Brownian trace on [0,1] equal to one almost surely?
statement_caveat: A nontrivial arc contains at least two distinct points. The lower bound one alone is not a solution.
title: Percolation dimension of a planar Brownian trace

statement: In any acute triangle, can reflected Brownian motions from distinct starting points be coupled so their meeting-time tail decays at every exponential rate strictly below the first positive Neumann spectral rate?
statement_caveat: Check the generator convention in Burdzy-Kendall (2000): the page calls its rate a Laplacian eigenvalue. A factor-two convention discrepancy is not a solution of the coupling question.
title: Efficient reflected-Brownian coupling in acute triangles

statement: Does some bounded connected smooth planar domain admit synchronously coupled reflected Brownian motions whose distance has positive limsup with positive probability?
statement_caveat: The page states that any such domain must have at least two holes by existing results.
title: Failure of synchronous contraction in a bounded planar domain

statement: For synchronously coupled reflected Brownian motions in the exterior of a nondegenerate closed disk, can their distance have positive limsup with positive probability?
statement_caveat: This unbounded exterior geometry differs from the bounded-domain existence question.
title: Synchronous reflection outside a disk

statement: For N>=3 Brownian particles in any bounded open connected domain, killed at the boundary and immediately cloned from a uniformly selected survivor, are the successive death times almost surely non-accumulating?
statement_caveat: N=2 is explicitly reported solved by Kwasnicki (2024). The earlier general proof had an irreparable error; it is not admissible evidence for the general result.
title: Non-explosion of Fleming-Viot Brownian particles in arbitrary domains

statement: If reflected Brownian motions in a bounded connected domain can remain a positive distance apart forever with positive probability, must there be such a coupling with one path a fixed deterministic function of the other at each time?
statement_caveat: Regularity sufficient to define the intended reflected Brownian motion needs to be fixed from the cited background. A metric-graph counterexample on the page is not a Euclidean-domain counterexample.
title: Rigidity of shy reflected-Brownian couplings

statement: Concatenate independent Brownian path segments cut at stopping times indexed by all integers, with lengths uniformly bounded by a deterministic constant and divergent sums in both directions. Is the resulting path two-sided Brownian after some random time shift?
statement_caveat: The paper's related backward-Brownian question and its almost-sure random bound are recorded as related variants, not an extra count. Independent lengths alone are not the same as stopping times depending on their Brownian paths.
title: Bounded independent Brownian pieces and two-sided Brownian motion

statement: Uniformly label an n-by-n square grid and condition on exactly two local maxima. Does their graph distance divided by n converge in distribution to zero?
statement_caveat: This is the literal displayed question, despite the heading about repulsion. Verify against Twin peaks (2020) before correcting the sign or reporting a counterexample.
title: Separation of two peaks in random square-grid labelings

statement: Does a decomposable forward Brownian motion which is also backward Brownian necessarily become two-sided Brownian after a random shift? The source also asks weaker related formulations using independence of past and future at a random time.
statement_caveat: The three linked formulations are grouped as one compatibility problem. A general process that is both forward and backward Brownian without the extra assumptions is already counterexampled in the paper.
title: Compatibility of forward and backward Brownian decompositions

statement: In a two-sided independent concatenation, use unit-length Brownian segments except at increasingly rare negative-time indices where segments stop on first hitting -1. Characterize frequencies giving backward or two-sided Brownian motion.
statement_caveat: The exact deterministic or random schedule is part of the classification; do not invent a schedule and count it as another sourced question.
title: Sparse first-passage pieces in a forward Brownian concatenation

statement: Start at the origin in Z^2; after first visiting a site step horizontally with either sign equally likely, and after a repeat visit step vertically with either sign equally likely. Does any site receive infinitely many visits with positive probability?
statement_caveat: The source indexing omits the first step; use its intended new-site rule also at time zero. The analogous four- and three-dimensional results do not decide this planar model.
title: Recurrence of the planar horizontal-new vertical-old walk

statement: For a Cayley graph of exponential growth rate b and 1<lambda<b, does the distance from the identity divided by time for RW_lambda converge almost surely to a strictly positive speed?
statement_caveat: RW_lambda uses the source's radial conductances, favoring motion toward the identity for lambda>1. The case lambda=1 may have zero speed and is excluded.
title: Positive speed of inward-biased walks below the Cayley growth rate

statement: If T is any geodesic spanning tree rooted at the identity of a Cayley graph of growth rate b, must br(T)=b, equivalently must its Bernoulli bond percolation threshold be 1/b?
statement_caveat: The branching-number/percolation equivalence is a theorem of the source. The question is stated there geometrically; its probability formulation is recorded transparently. Lexicographically minimal spanning trees satisfy it.
title: Percolation threshold on arbitrary geodesic Cayley spanning trees

statement: For increasing events A,B on edge subsets, is the probability of their disjoint occurrence under any weighted uniform spanning-tree law at most P(A)P(B)?
statement_caveat: Disjoint witnesses use disjoint edge-coordinate sets. Arbitrary events are excluded; negative association for fixed disjoint coordinates is weaker. Goldman 2023 proves a special class generated by simple points.
title: BK disjoint occurrence for weighted uniform spanning trees

statement: Is every infinite Bernoulli percolation cluster on a transient Cayley graph almost surely transient?
statement_caveat: The claim concerns all infinite clusters simultaneously. Nonamenable and Euclidean cases have substantial existing results.
title: Transience preserved in Cayley percolation clusters

statement: Does simple random walk on a Cayley graph have positive speed if and only if simple random walk on its infinite Bernoulli percolation clusters has positive speed almost surely?
statement_caveat: Use graph distance in the cluster for the cluster speed as in the source context; compare with ambient speed carefully. Nonamenable cases are reported known.
title: Positive-speed equivalence for Cayley percolation clusters

statement: Does every locally finite quasi-transitive graph with exactly one end have Bernoulli percolation uniqueness threshold p_u<1?
statement_caveat: A one-ended finite-presentation class is known. The assertion p_c<1 alone is weaker and now resolved in the transitive setting.
title: Uniqueness threshold below one in one-ended transitive graphs

statement: Must p_c(G)<p_u(G) for every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph? The source's related formulation asks whether the property p_c<p_u is preserved by rough isometries among quasi-transitive graphs.
statement_caveat: The closely linked rough-isometry conjecture is grouped here to avoid counting a reformulation separately. Nonunimodular and many other cases are established.
title: Nonuniqueness phase for nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs

statement: Is a finitely generated group amenable exactly when every Cayley graph from every finite generating set has bootstrap complete-occupation critical probability p(G,k) in {0,1} for every threshold k?
statement_caveat: Initially each vertex is occupied independently with probability p; vacant vertices with at least k occupied neighbors become occupied. Criticality is for positive probability of eventual occupation of all vertices.
title: Bootstrap thresholds as a characterization of amenable groups

statement: If G is quasi-transitive and p_c(G)<1, is there almost surely no infinite Bernoulli cluster at p_c(G)?
statement_caveat: Do not count each lattice dimension as a separate problem. Known nonamenable and high-dimensional cases do not settle the entire assertion.
title: Absence of infinite clusters at critical percolation

statement: For an infinite network, is there a coupling (W,F) of its wired and free uniform spanning forests with W subset F almost surely whose joint law is invariant under all network automorphisms?
statement_caveat: Strassen gives an unconstrained monotone coupling. Sofic Cayley groups admit invariant couplings by Lyons-Thom 2016; arbitrary invariant percolations can fail this property.
title: Invariant monotone coupling of free and wired uniform spanning forests

statement: For a Cayley graph of a finitely presented group, is the expected degree at the identity in its free uniform spanning forest rational?
statement_caveat: This is the first l2-Betti-number question via E degree=2+2 beta_1. Counterexamples to broader Atiyah statements must be checked for both first degree and finite presentation before exclusion.
title: Rational expected free-forest degree for finitely presented groups

statement: For any Cayley graph, its free uniform spanning forest F, and epsilon>0, is there an invariant connected random spanning subgraph omega containing F with P(e in omega minus F)<epsilon for every edge e?
statement_caveat: Added edges may depend on F. Independent Bernoulli sprinkling is explicitly known to fail for some nonamenable graphs.
title: Connecting a free uniform spanning forest by arbitrarily sparse invariant additions

statement: On every infinite connected locally finite network, is the number of free uniform spanning-forest components almost surely a constant?
statement_caveat: Automorphisms with an infinite orbit give a positive answer. The remaining arbitrary-network setting lacks that ergodic shortcut.
title: Deterministic component count of the free uniform spanning forest

statement: On every transitive network, is the free uniform spanning forest almost surely connected or composed of infinitely many components?
statement_caveat: The unimodular case was solved by Hutchcroft-Nachmias 2017 and Timar 2018. The unresolved scope retained here is nonunimodular.
title: One or infinitely many free-forest components without unimodularity

statement: On a transitive network with distinct free and wired uniform spanning-forest laws, must every free-forest component have infinitely many ends almost surely?
statement_caveat: The source's subsequent indistinguishability theorem settles the unimodular case. Haar-light components alone do not automatically refute an ends statement.
title: Infinitely many ends in all free-forest components without unimodularity

statement: If the wired and free uniform spanning-forest measures differ on an infinite network, must they be mutually singular?
statement_caveat: Known for trees and networks with an infinite automorphism orbit. Distinct probability measures need not be singular in general.
title: Singularity of distinct free and wired forest measures

statement: For both free and wired uniform spanning forests of an arbitrary infinite network, is the event that every component has one end of probability zero or one?
statement_caveat: Both boundary conditions are grouped. Changing finitely many forest edges can merge components, so tail measurability needs a proof.
title: Zero-one law for all forest components having one end

statement: Along the unique ray from the identity in its wired uniform spanning-forest component, do the finite bushes at successive ray vertices, translated back to the identity, converge in distribution?
statement_caveat: Restrict to Cayley graphs where the stated unique ray exists. The source records solutions for growth at least five and standard Z^2,Z^3,Z^4; the remaining low-growth Cayley cases must be checked individually before any promotion.
title: Limiting bushes along a wired uniform-forest ray

statement: Does each wired minimal spanning-forest component of a nonunimodular transitive graph have one end almost surely?
statement_caveat: The accompanying request for useful nonhomogeneous sufficient conditions is retained as a related extension, not another count.
title: One-ended wired minimal forests without unimodularity

statement: If a quasi-transitive graph has distinct wired and free minimal spanning-forest laws, does every free minimal-forest component have infinitely many ends almost surely?
statement_caveat: The source and later Timar results establish unimodular cases; retain the genuinely remaining scope. All edges have independent continuous labels.
title: Infinitely many ends in free minimal forests distinct from wired

statement: On a nonamenable quasi-transitive graph with p_u<1, is the free minimal spanning forest connected almost surely exactly when Bernoulli percolation has a unique infinite cluster at p_u?
statement_caveat: The source's stronger bijection between forest components and p_u clusters is grouped as a strengthening. One direction is already proved there.
title: Minimal-forest connectivity and uniqueness at p_u

statement: Must both free and wired minimal spanning forests on a quasi-transitive graph have either one or infinitely many components almost surely?
statement_caveat: Free and wired are grouped. Distinct-law unimodular cases are reported resolved by Timar 2018.
title: One or infinitely many minimal-forest components

statement: For a Cayley graph with p_u<1, is there an implication in either direction between multiple infinite clusters at p_u and the nonexistence of an invariant random spanning tree?
statement_caveat: Each condition implies the free minimal spanning forest is disconnected, but a common consequence does not establish either implication.
title: Uniqueness-critical percolation versus invariant spanning trees

statement: Are the components of both free and wired minimal spanning forests on a unimodular transitive graph indistinguishable by every invariant Borel component property?
statement_caveat: Timar 2018 settles the free case when free and wired differ. The remaining equal-law or wired scope is the target.
title: Indistinguishability of minimal spanning-forest components

statement: For a Cayley graph not roughly isometric to Z, does the sequence of translated bushes along a ray in the identity's wired minimal spanning-forest component converge in distribution?
statement_caveat: Uniqueness of that ray is itself tied to critical percolation. Keep the conditional structural assumptions explicit rather than selecting an unmentioned canonical ray.
title: Limiting bushes along a wired minimal-forest ray

statement: For which dimensions d is the minimal spanning forest on Z^d connected almost surely?
statement_caveat: Competing predictions put a transition near dimension six or eight. These dimension variants form one classification problem.
title: Dimensions with a connected Euclidean minimal spanning forest

statement: Does the minimal spanning tree on epsilon Z^2 have a full distributional scaling limit as epsilon tends to zero, in the embedded-tree topology used for its known subsequential limits?
statement_caveat: The source leaves the exact topology to the cited Aizenman-Burchard-Newman-Wilson framework. A triangular-lattice theorem does not settle square-lattice universality.
title: Full scaling limit of the square-lattice minimal spanning tree

statement: If a connected locally finite graph is roughly isometric to a tree, must its free minimal spanning forest be connected almost surely?
statement_caveat: This concerns minimal forests, not uniform forests; Pete-Timar's uniform-forest counterexample cannot be substituted.
title: Connectivity of minimal forests on graphs roughly isometric to trees

statement: For the middle-thirds Cantor set E, let nu_b be harmonic measure on the source's base-b coding tree T[b](E), pushed to E. Is nu_2 mutually singular with the Cantor-Lebesgue measure nu_3?
statement_caveat: Use the coding-tree construction and boundary map in Section 16.2; distinct harmonic measures or dimensions alone do not prove singularity.
title: Singularity of binary and ternary harmonic codings of the Cantor set

statement: For a nondegenerate supercritical Galton-Watson law of mean m under the chapter's moment assumptions, must every consistent equivariant flow rule different almost surely from UNIF have boundary-measure Hausdorff dimension below log m almost surely?
statement_caveat: The source proves a stationary-measure sufficient condition. Difference on a GW-null set is not an admissible counterexample.
title: Dimension drop for every nonuniform Galton-Watson flow

statement: For a nondegenerate supercritical Galton-Watson tree without leaves and 0<=lambda<m, does harmonic-measure dimension of RW_lambda increase with lambda, and is the increase strict?
statement_caveat: On a deterministic regular tree the dimension is constant, so retain the chapter's nondegeneracy assumptions for strictness. Both monotonic and strict clauses are grouped.
title: Monotonicity of harmonic dimension under inward bias

statement: For Galton-Watson trees with p_0=0, is the speed of RW_lambda nonincreasing as the bias parameter lambda increases?
statement_caveat: The transient range is 0<lambda<m; beyond criticality the speed is zero. Positive-regeneration and large-bias partial results are not the complete monotonicity claim.
title: Monotonicity of biased-walk speed on Galton-Watson trees

statement: Prove that every continuous iid passage-time law with a compact limit shape has a uniform constant C>0 such that 1-mu(z)>=C min(mu(z-z1),mu(z-z2))^2 for boundary points z1,z2 and z=(1-lambda)z1+lambda z2.

statement: Determine whether the dimension-dependent passage-time fluctuation exponent chi(d) tends to zero as d tends to infinity.

title: High-dimensional limit of the FPP fluctuation exponent

statement: Show that two independent geodesics from0 to ne1, sampled in independent iid planar environments with the same law, have expected edge overlap at least n^a for some a>0.
statement_caveat: Independent environments and a fixed measurable geodesic-selection rule are intended; two samples in one unique-geodesic environment would be identical.
title: Polynomial overlap of independent planar FPP geodesics

statement: For iid edge times0 with probability p_c(Z^3) and1 otherwise, determine whether E T(0,boundary B(n)) is comparable to log n.
statement_caveat: The target is undirected edge FPP at the three-dimensional bond threshold; planar critical exponents cannot be transferred.
title: Critical Bernoulli FPP growth in three dimensions

statement: Determine the largest power alpha for which standardized passage times constrained to Z times[-n^alpha,n^alpha]^(d-1) converge to a standard normal law.
statement_caveat: The source defines gamma_F(d) by this threshold under a finite2+delta edge-time moment. A sufficient exponent from the source theorem is not an optimality result.
title: Sharp width threshold for the thin-cylinder FPP CLT

statement: For every iid finite nonnegative passage-time distribution in d>=3, prove that the infimum over finite paths between any two vertices is attained.
statement_caveat: Infinite passage-time edges are not included in this formulation. Non-iid weighted graphs can fail attainment and therefore cannot settle the iid question by analogy.
title: Existence of finite FPP geodesics without distributional assumptions

statement: Exhibit a nondegenerate iid undirected FPP law with well-defined fluctuation and wandering exponents satisfying chi=2xi-1.
statement_caveat: Conditional proofs assuming suitably strong exponents exist do not exhibit a law for which those assumptions hold. Exactly solvable directed last-passage models are outside the target.
title: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation

statement: Prove that continuous iid planar passage-time distributions have infinitely many pairwise eventually disjoint geodesic rays; the source also asks for an example outside the percolation-cone class.
statement_caveat: The universal continuous-law question and its weaker example target are grouped. Distinct rays mean sharing at most finitely many vertices, not merely having different first edges.
title: Infinitely many planar FPP geodesic rays for continuous laws

statement: For iid passage-time laws with unique finite geodesics, determine whether the geodesics from0 to ne1 converge locally to a single infinite ray as n tends to infinity.
statement_caveat: Convergence means stabilization of every finite initial segment. Existence of some subsequential ray is strictly weaker.
title: Full-sequence convergence of FPP geodesics to a ray

statement: In uniquely geodesic planar iid FPP, prove that no fixed vertex belongs to geodesics from-ne1 to ne1 for infinitely many n.
statement_caveat: This is the stronger almost-sure formulation printed in the survey. The known BKS result that the probability of midpoint membership tends to zero is not by itself this statement.
title: Almost-sure escape from a fixed midpoint in FPP

statement: Show that every deterministic direction belongs to the Licea-Newman full-measure set D: from a fixed lattice vertex there are almost surely not two distinct geodesic rays with that direction.
statement_caveat: The axial case and all-direction case are grouped. This is at-most-one, not an assertion that a ray in that direction exists. The null event may depend on the fixed direction.
title: Uniqueness of planar directional geodesics in every fixed direction

statement: Extend the planar coalescence conclusion to higher dimensions: for a fixed direction with almost-sure uniqueness of a directional ray from each vertex, must directional rays from different vertices coalesce?
statement_caveat: The source asks whether its two-dimensional theorem extends. The relevant directional-uniqueness hypothesis must be stated rather than silently assumed in higher dimensions.
title: Coalescence of directional FPP rays in higher dimensions

statement: Let f(r) count edges meeting the Euclidean circle of radius r that belong to infinitely many finite geodesics from0. Determine whether f(r) tends to infinity, and at what rate.
statement_caveat: Assume a unique rooted finite-geodesic tree. Source questions about how many rays exist and this radial growth function are related but the latter requests additional spatial rate information.
title: Growth of the infinite-descendant part of the FPP geodesic tree

statement: For nondegenerate continuous iid planar passage-time laws in the usual positive-speed regime, determine whether a bi-infinite geodesic exists.
statement_caveat: The survey's short question sits in the uniquely geodesic random setting. Deterministic equal weights and the one-dimensional lattice have obvious geodesic lines and do not resolve the intended planar question.
title: Absence of bi-infinite geodesics in planar iid FPP

locator: Question33, PDF p.130; model definition pp.128-129
statement: Prove that the Eden model's limit shape is not a Euclidean ball in the dimensions left open by existing high-dimensional results, in particular dimension2.
statement_caveat: The source defines an Eden version choosing a boundary vertex uniformly. Edge-exponential infection generally chooses vertices at rates proportional to infected neighbors; these versions must not be identified without checking the time change.
title: Noncircular low-dimensional Eden limit shape

statement: Show that two-type Richardson growth on Z^d, d>=2, from distinct finite seeds cannot coexist indefinitely at unequal infection speeds; establish the proposed monotonicity in relative speed if that route is valid.
statement_caveat: The source assumes an ordering of the two parameters before asking monotonicity. Speed versus mean-passage-time conventions must be fixed. The universal noncoexistence and monotonicity route are grouped.
title: Noncoexistence of unequal-speed Richardson infections

statement: Characterize the pairs of iid half-plane edge laws F_minus,F_plus for which vertical growth along their interface is strictly faster than in either homogeneous model.
statement_caveat: Greater speed means a smaller directional time constant. The exact convention for edges on the interface must be fixed; finite detours in the constant-law check below do not affect its conclusion.
title: Strict interface speedup in half-plane inhomogeneous FPP

current_status_note: Historical open statement checked; later-literature scope retained in caveat
statement: Establish Gaussian-free-field scaling and SLE4 interface limits for the source's uniform odd-integer triangular-lattice heights, and for its uniform real-valued Lipschitz heights with the appropriate boundary amplitude.
statement_caveat: The two genuinely different height ensembles are conservatively grouped as one universality family. Integer heights have nearest-neighbor difference0 or2 and boundary values plus/minus1; real heights have difference at most1 and tuned boundary values plus/minus lambda.
title: Uniform Lipschitz height models and their interfaces

current_status_note: Historical open statement checked; later-literature scope retained in caveat
statement: Project a planar Dirichlet Gaussian free field onto Laplace eigenmodes with eigenvalue magnitude at most R, add the harmonic extension of suitably chosen two-arc boundary values, and prove that the connecting zero interface converges to SLE4 as R tends to infinity.
statement_caveat: The cutoff is spectral and nonlocal. Distributional convergence of the field itself is already built into the construction and is not the requested interface convergence.
title: SLE4 from spectral truncations of the Gaussian free field

current_status_note: Historical open statement checked; later-literature scope retained in caveat

current_status_note: Historical open statement checked; later-literature scope retained in caveat

statement_caveat: The q=2 FK-Ising case is already resolved and excluded from the unresolved scope. Square bond percolation is q=1 and is grouped here instead of being counted again as Problem2.11.

current_status_note: Historical open statement checked; later-literature scope retained in caveat

statement_caveat: A uniform embedded n-vertex tree is not a uniform spanning tree of a fixed region or a critical Galton-Watson tree. High-dimensional spread-out results do not settle the planar model.

current_status_note: Historical open statement checked; later-literature scope retained in caveat

current_status_note: Historical open statement checked; later-literature scope retained in caveat

statement_caveat: Literally, the zero measure is sigma-finite; the source context requires a useful nonzero measure. Rezaei proves that the critical power gauge r^(1+kappa/8) gives zero Hausdorff measure. Minkowski content is not automatically a Hausdorff measure.
title: A nontrivial exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE

current_status_note: Current primary2026 source explicitly asks this; exhaustive later-resolution search not certified

statement_caveat: Global noninjectivity is already noted by the authors. The question concerns typical fibers in the specified support. It is related to, but stronger than, recovering only the SLE path measurably.
title: Almost-sure fibers of chronological loop addition

current_status_note: Current primary2026 source explicitly asks this; exhaustive later-resolution search not certified
statement: Extend the chronological loop-decoration representation to the three-dimensional scaling limit of loop-erased random walk, yielding the full parametrized Brownian path rather than only equality of random ranges.

statement: Describe a unit Brownian loop as an SLE2-type loop decorated by an independent Brownian loop soup, with a precise law and chronology.
statement_caveat: A closed loop has no distinguished endpoint ordering. Rooting conventions, duration conditioning, and the law of the proposed SLE loop must be fixed together.

statement_caveat: Only parameters giving a nonnegative soup intensity and an applicable attachment construction are meaningful. The interval2<=kappa<=8/3 interpolates the Brownian kappa2 endpoint and undecorated SLE8/3 endpoint.

current_status_note: Current primary2026 source explicitly asks this; exhaustive later-resolution search not certified
