title: Rough-path continuity of chronological loop attachment

later_resolution.finding: Corrected law is indirectly identified; direct marking proof supplied here is not counted as a new theorem

locator: Open Problem4.1, PDF p.210; equations4.5.5 and4.5.20
statement: Explain directly how mixing the heavy-tailed degree weights yields the independent-increment iid-degree exploration limit.
statement_caveat: The deterministic drift in the short2017 formulation must be replaced by the random critical shift Lambda_0. Dhara et al2019 equation2.22 and Remark11 already identify the corrected law indirectly.
title: Random critical drift in the annealed thinned Levy process

statement: For affine preferential attachment with m>=2 and delta>0, prove convergence of typical graph distance/log n and diameter/log n to explicit positive constants a<b.
statement_caveat: Two-sided logarithmic bounds are weaker than convergence to constants. The positive-delta regime is the finite-variance degree regime; logarithmic-logarithmic formulas from negative delta do not apply.
title: First-order distance constants in finite-variance preferential attachment

statement: Determine the centered fluctuation scales and limiting laws for typical distances and diameter in affine preferential-attachment graphs with m>=2.
statement_caveat: Parameter regimes are one source problem, not separate corpus variants. Tightness and full-sequence convergence must be distinguished because graph distances are integer-valued.
title: Fluctuations of preferential-attachment distances and diameter

statement: Determine fluctuations of the longest minimum-weight path, both from a fixed root and over all vertex pairs, beyond the first-order e log n and alpha_star log n scales.
statement_caveat: The rooted shortest-path tree is a random recursive tree, for which substantial height refinements already exist. The all-pairs fluctuation target is retained; known rooted results are not new solutions.
title: Second-order extremal hopcount in exponential complete-graph FPP

statement: Describe the fluctuations of the minimal total weight between two typical vertices of an infinite-variance configuration model when the associated weighted branching process is conservative.
statement_caveat: The source explicitly says the question concerns random fluctuations beyond the leading quantile-sum scale. Later leading-order weighted-distance results must not be mistaken for a complete centered limiting law.
title: Conservative weighted-distance fluctuations in heavy-tailed configuration models

statement: Determine the scaling and possible central limit laws for the number of edges on a minimum-weight path between typical vertices of an infinite-variance configuration model.
statement_caveat: The target is hopcount, not total weight or unweighted distance. Separate edge-weight laws may lead to different behaviors but are one classification problem.
title: Hopcount universality in infinite-variance weighted configuration models

locator: Open Problem3.4, PDF p.149 and discussion p.154
statement: Complete the classification of complete-graph first-passage percolation with varying edge-weight distributions, including the strong-disorder regime related to the minimum spanning tree.
statement_caveat: The source highlights weights E_e raised to s_n and the regimes not covered by its theorem. A value comparison with a bottleneck problem does not prove convergence of path geometry.
title: Weak-to-strong disorder universality in complete-graph FPP

statement: Identify centered fluctuation laws for exponential-weight flooding time and weighted diameter in the configuration-model regimes of Theorem3.37.
statement_caveat: The source assumes a convergent degree law with a uniformly bounded2+epsilon moment and positive mass at the minimum degree. If the graph is disconnected, distances must be restricted to the relevant giant component; infinite distances are not silently included.
title: Fluctuations of weighted flooding and diameter on configuration models

statement: Extend weighted flooding-time and diameter asymptotics from exponential weights to general iid nonnegative edge-weight laws on the configuration model.
statement_caveat: Both the lower tail used by fast paths and the upper tail of the minimum weight leaving a peripheral vertex can matter. This is one law-classification problem.
title: General edge-weight laws for random-graph flooding and diameter

statement: Determine the first-order extreme hopcount from one root and over all pairs for general configuration-model degree laws, and extend beyond exponential edge weights.
statement_caveat: The known regular-graph constants use a branching-generation large-deviation calculation. Replacing the degree by its mean is not justified for extremes.
title: Extreme hopcounts for general random-graph degree and weight laws

statement: Remove the extra degree restrictions used to upgrade heavy-tailed critical configuration-model components from Gromov-weak convergence to Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov convergence.
statement_caveat: The printed problem heading says finite third moment, but its referenced theorem and surrounding text concern infinite third moment, tau in(3,4). Bhamidi et al2020 improve the global lower-mass bound under slightly stronger assumptions; the minimal-assumption remainder requires exact comparison.
title: Minimal assumptions for heavy-tailed critical metric convergence

statement: For affine preferential attachment with a fixed m>=2 edges per arriving vertex and delta>0, identify the percolation scaling window and largest critical component sizes.
statement_caveat: The percolation threshold itself is covered by later work2312.14085. The2025 growing-graph window theorem concerns models with independently attached edges; it is not automatically the fixed-outdegree model asked here.
title: Critical window for fixed-outdegree preferential attachment

statement: Characterize critical component universality for general inhomogeneous random-graph kernels, including the proposed role of the positive principal eigenfunction belonging to L3.
statement_caveat: The general question and the eigenfunction criterion are grouped. Rank-one and finite-type theorems do not cover every irreducible unbounded kernel.
title: Kernel criteria for critical inhomogeneous random-graph universality

statement: Identify the critical time for percolation of the vacant set left after a random walk runs for order n time on a configuration model, including degree laws with diverging second moment.
statement_caveat: Time normalization, the giant component, and initial distribution must match the source. The suggestion that the threshold vanishes for infinite second moment is a question, not an established consequence of ordinary percolation.
title: Vacant-set percolation threshold on general configuration models

statement: Obtain metric-space scaling limits for the largest critical vacant-set components of general configuration models, including heavy-tailed degree sequences.
statement_caveat: Random-regular vacant-set metric limits are already established. The general degree law and possible suppression of high-degree hubs form the unresolved extension.
title: Metric scaling of critical random-walk vacant components

statement: For nearest-neighbor percolation on growing d-dimensional tori with fixed d>6 in the critical window around p_c(Z^d), prove convergence of the ordered component sizes to the appropriate shifted and rescaled multiplicative-coalescent law.
statement_caveat: Correct window centering and constants are part of the source question. Results for a growing-dimensional hypercube, or order-of-magnitude estimates, are not automatically this fixed-d torus theorem.
title: Erdos-Renyi component-size limits for high-dimensional tori

statement: Identify and prove the metric-measure scaling limits of minimum spanning trees on configuration models with minimum limiting degree at least3, across finite-third-moment and heavy-tailed degree regimes.
statement_caveat: The two source regimes are grouped. The random3-regular case is resolved by Addario-Berry and Sen1810.03802; it is excluded from the open remainder. The law of iid continuous edge weights is not an extra family of distinct problems.
title: Configuration-model minimum spanning-tree metric limits

statement: Under convergence of third degree moments, prove that the largest barely subcritical configuration-model component has order max{d_max/epsilon_n, epsilon_n^(-2)log(n epsilon_n^3)} in the regime specified by the source.
statement_caveat: The asymptotic regime must have epsilon_n tending to0 with n epsilon_n^3 large; otherwise the displayed logarithm is not the intended barely-subcritical scale. Infinite-third-moment results are a different regime.
title: Two competing largest-component scales in barely subcritical configuration models

statement: Prove that the susceptibility critical exponent gamma_prime on the ordered side of the locally tree-like ferromagnetic Ising transition equals1 under the source's degree assumptions.
statement_caveat: The high-temperature exponent gamma=1 and the random-regular ordered-phase case are already known. The source seeks the missing upper bound for general degree laws with a nontrivial finite critical inverse temperature.
title: Ordered-phase susceptibility exponent on random trees and graphs

statement: Extend the critical non-classical total-spin limit theorem from annealed generalized random graphs to quenched configuration models or quenched generalized random graphs.
statement_caveat: Quenched means fixing the sampled graph before taking its spin law. Matching critical exponents or annealed pressure does not establish a quenched distributional limit.
title: Quenched non-Gaussian critical spin limits on heterogeneous random graphs

statement: Prove metastable behavior of low-temperature ferromagnetic Ising dynamics on configuration models as n tends to infinity with inverse temperature fixed and large.
statement_caveat: The source contrasts this with taking temperature to0 at fixed n. Later random-regular metastability results are known; the full general configuration-model extension is retained.
title: Fixed-temperature metastability for general configuration models

statement: Extend the ferromagnetic Potts Bethe free-energy and phase-diagram results from regular locally tree-like graphs to general configuration-model degree laws.
statement_caveat: Can and van der Hofstad2503.17636 establish additional regular-graph and parameter-region results. A lower Bethe bound is not equality throughout the general heterogeneous phase diagram.
title: Potts free energy for general configuration-model degrees

statement: Bound the Shannon entropy of the squared Fourier coefficients of every Boolean function by a universal constant times its total influence.
statement_caveat: The weaker min-entropy formulation is grouped here. Gonzalez,MacManus,Pereyra2606.00246 still calls the full statement a conjecture and proves additional classes.
title: Fourier entropy versus total influence

statement: For a size-s DNF, concentrate all but epsilon of its squared Fourier mass on at most s raised to O(log(1/epsilon)) coefficients.
statement_caveat: The weaker polynomial-in-s formulation is grouped. Lecomte-Tan2109.04525 improve read-dependent bounds, not the full assertion.
title: Polynomial Fourier concentration for DNF formulas

locator: Section1.4, Conjecture1; O-Donnell2012 p.5 weaker consequences
statement: For an unbiased linear threshold f and rho in(0,1), prove Stab_rho(f)>=(2/pi)*arcsin(rho).
statement_caveat: This is the authors refined conjecture, not the false finite-majority comparison. The degree-one Fourier lower bound2/pi and small-noise consequence are grouped as parts of this family.

locator: PDF p.6, Optimality of Majorities for Non-Interactive Correlation Distillation
statement: When r independent noisy copies of a common uniform bit string use the same odd Boolean function, is the agreement probability maximized by majority on some odd subset of coordinates?
statement_caveat: The number of players and the noise parameter are one optimization problem. This differs from two-party erasure distillation and from minimizing threshold stability.
title: Optimal odd functions for many-player correlation distillation

statement: For f on the uniform discrete cube taking values in[-1,1] and having degree at most d, prove some L2 influence is at least(Var(f)/d)^C for a universal C.
statement_caveat: Bhattacharya2402.13952 and its March2026 revision concern random restrictions. That does not settle every original polynomial.

statement: For correlated standard Gaussian vectors with prescribed rho and set measures mu,nu, minimize P(X in A,Y in B) under central symmetry A=-A.
statement_caveat: The proposed centered-ball optimizer is not the general optimization question. Heilman1511.00382 gives negative results for ball/complement maximizers in dimension at least2; this does not identify every optimum.

statement: Prove that equal-volume regular-simplex partitions maximize Gaussian noise stability for positive correlation and minimize it for negative correlation, for every admissible number of cells.
statement_caveat: The signs of correlation and cell numbers form one source conjecture. Heilman2608.00333 claims a substantial three-cell correlation range; it does not cover all cell counts or every positive correlation.
title: Noise-optimal equal-volume Gaussian partitions

locator: PDF p.9, Linear Coefficients versus Total Degree

statement_caveat: The stronger and weaker proposed constants are grouped. Jha1611.01029 and Wang2020/002 discuss partial cases and reformulations; neither title is treated as a complete resolution.

locator: PDF p.9, k-wise Independence for PTFs
statement: Determine the smallest k(d,epsilon) for which every k-wise independent standard-Gaussian vector fools every degree-d polynomial threshold to error epsilon.
statement_caveat: The joint distribution of every k coordinates must be product Gaussian. Matching finitely many mixed moments alone is a weaker property and is not substituted for this assumption.

statement_caveat: The2025 Generalised Linial-Nisan counterexample controls marginals of bounded-size coordinate sets; its theorem alone does not assert small bias for every parity. It is not treated as a resolution of this different source statement.
title: Polynomial small bias sufficient to fool DNF events

statement: For unbiased Boolean f and coordinate-retention probability p in(0,1/2), prove E|E[f(X) given the retained coordinates]|<=(2/pi)*arcsin(sqrt(p)).
statement_caveat: The false finite-majority comparator is excluded. This is the2026 authors refined conjecture. Requiring the optimizing second output to be unbiased is a distinct constraint; the source formulation here uses the absolute conditional expectation.
title: Sharp erasure-distillation bound from the Gaussian limit

statement: Prove total influence at most C*d*sqrt(n), or at least C_d*sqrt(n), for every degree-d polynomial threshold function on n uniform bits.
statement_caveat: The exact symmetric-maximizer conjecture is false, with Chapman2108.02288 giving later counterexamples. The weaker asymptotic bounds explicitly posed in the source are grouped here.
title: Asymptotic influence bounds for polynomial thresholds

locator: Problem 3.3, arXiv PDF p.6; journal p.359
statement: Find the optimal universal C such that every compactly supported law mu becomes unimodal after free convolution with the variance-t semicircle law for all t >= C times the square of its support diameter.
statement_caveat: The source prints 2<=C<=4, but its own symmetric-Bernoulli threshold t=4 and diameter 2 imply only C>=1. The candidate proof derives both bounds independently. Manuscript header 2021 differs from the arXiv revision date 2018.

statement: Is the free additive convolution of two symmetric unimodal probability laws unimodal?
statement_caveat: The older AIM free-analysis question is the same family and is not counted again. A semicircle factor and some freely infinitely divisible subclasses are established cases.
title: Symmetric unimodality under free addition

statement: Does a non-point-mass law exist whose free additive convolution with every unimodal law is unimodal?
statement_caveat: The source already excludes all nondegenerate finite-variance laws. The remaining possible examples must have infinite variance.
title: Existence of nontrivial freely strongly unimodal laws

statement: Estimate the mode of classical Brownian motion started from a law with a finite exponential quadratic moment, and determine analogous estimates for free Brownian motion.
statement_caveat: The source gives a growing interval of radius sqrt(t)/2 once unimodality holds. Classical and free versions of this mode-location request are grouped.
title: Location of Brownian modes at large time

statement: For a classical or free strictly alpha-stable process, alpha in(0,2), does a finite absolute(2+alpha)-moment of the initial law ensure eventual unimodality under the corresponding convolution?
statement_caveat: Use the published wording: classical convolution with classical stable laws, free convolution with free stable laws. The archived preprint wording differs. All stability indices are one source conjecture; the Cauchy case is already established.
title: Critical moment condition for eventual stable-process unimodality

statement: Do uniformly sampled permutation pairs satisfying U^2*V^2=V*U converge strongly, after removing the common constant vector, to the regular representation of the Gieseking group?
statement_caveat: Surface groups are already covered by the source. The later2602.11905 free-product theorem concerns a different relation and does not settle this hyperbolic3-manifold group.
title: Uniform permutation representations of the Gieseking group

statement: For a fixed number of uniform random generators of S_N, do all nontrivial eigenvalues apart from the sign representation approach the free-group spectral bound? Develop the associated high-dimensional representation convergence.
statement_caveat: The weaker expansion question and the stronger arbitrary-irrep formulation are grouped with the optimal-gap family. The trivial and sign representations must both be removed.
title: Optimal spectra of random symmetric-group Cayley graphs

statement: Find finite-group sequences whose fixed-number uniform random Cayley generators have asymptotically optimal nontrivial spectral gap, particularly finite special linear groups.

result_status: PARTIALLY ANSWERED, and this row is the codex ledger's copy of intake I row I0084, the same Conjecture 5.5 of Hasebe and Ueda. The compactly supported case of the CLASSICAL half is now a theorem with an explicit threshold. General criterion: for a symmetric density p, smooth and positive with p' < 0 on (0, infinity), put psi(x) = -(log|p'(x)|)' = -p''(x)/p'(x). Then every mu whose support has diameter at most D has mu * p unimodal IF AND ONLY IF psi(a)+psi(b) <= 0 for all a,b>0 with a+b <= D. The two conditions at a separating local minimum are linear in the measure, so Choquet puts the extreme points on at most two atoms; for a pair at -a and b the stationarity condition gives w1|p'(a)| = w2|p'(b)| and the curvature condition becomes exactly psi(a)+psi(b) >= 0, while the converse direction uses that same pair as a counterexample. Since psi scales, each kernel has a constant c(p) with unimodality guaranteed whenever D < c(p)s. For the symmetric stable laws with characteristic function exp(-|u|^alpha), c(alpha) = 2.813, 2.596, 2.133, 1.577, 1.145, 0.682, 0.095 at alpha = 2, 1.8, 1.5, 1.2, 1.0, 0.8, 0.5. So a compactly supported mu of diameter D has mu * S_t unimodal as soon as t > (D/c(alpha))^alpha. The conjecture's real content is unbounded support, where the criterion is silent because a+b is unbounded, which is why it carries a moment condition. The FREE half is untouched by this.
statement: For a classical or free strictly alpha-stable process, alpha in(0,2), does a finite absolute(2+alpha)-moment of the initial law ensure eventual unimodality under the corresponding convolution?
statement_caveat: Use the published wording: classical convolution with classical stable laws, free convolution with free stable laws. The archived preprint wording differs. All stability indices are one source conjecture; the Cauchy case is already established.
title: Critical moment condition for eventual stable-process unimodality

result_status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. The problem asks to improve the critical triangular-lattice one-arm probability from R^{-5/48+o(1)} to sharp multiplicative asymptotics, or at least to bounds by constant multiples. Du, Gao, Li and Zhuang, 'Sharp asymptotics for arm probabilities in critical planar percolation' (arXiv:2205.15901, 2022), obtain sharp asymptotics for half-plane j-arm events for every j >= 1 and for planar polychromatic j-arm events with j > 1, answering a large part of Schramm's 2006 question. Their abstract explicitly scopes out the planar MONOCHROMATIC one-arm case, which is exactly the exponent -5/48 here, so the problem as posed stands.
statement: Improve the critical triangular-percolation one-arm probability R^(-5/48+o(1)) to sharp multiplicative asymptotics, at least bounds by constant multiples of R^(-5/48).
statement_caveat: Du-Gao-Li-Zhuang resolve sharp half-plane and planar polychromatic multi-arm asymptotics; those resolved portions of the 2006 question are excluded. Their abstract does not include the planar one-arm event.

result_status: REFUTED for the loop-erasure rule, novelty not verified; OPEN for the uniform-geodesic rule. Take the six-vertex graph with edges N-u, u-x, x-F, N-v, v-y, y-F and the rung u-v (the Wheatstone bridge with both food-side edges subdivided once), whose two shortest N-F paths N-u-x-F and N-v-y-F have length 3. When each ant reinforces the loop erasure of its reversed walk, the rung's normalized weight converges to a positive limit with positive probability, so an edge on no shortest N-F path grows linearly. The September families of research7_2026-09-17/R7-02 keep the food-side edge single and do not contain this graph. Searched: Kious-Mailler-Schapira, Ann. Appl. Probab. 32(5) (2022), arXiv:2010.04820; arXiv:2106.10559 (a different rule); Mailler-Varin, arXiv:2601.22855 (January 2026, still states it as a conjecture). No published counterexample found.

result_status: REFUTED as displayed, novelty not verified: there are degree sequences meeting every hypothesis of the source (Condition 1.6, convergent third moments, p_2 < 1) with L_1 / max{d_max/epsilon_n, epsilon_n^(-2) log(n epsilon_n^3)} -> infinity in probability. Construction: M = m^(3K-2) hubs of degree m^2 with K = max(2, floor(sqrt(log m))), n = 8 m^(3K+5), and a bulk of degrees 1 and 3 tuned so that epsilon_n ~ 1/m; the hubs carry vanishing mass in every moment up to the third and still link through direct hub-hub edges. title: Uniform stationary normal approximation from gap and bounded observable
result_status: ANSWERED: no, novelty not verified. For b >= 1 and s >= 2b let X = (Y, V) on {0,1} x {-1,1} with Y and V independent: Y moves 0 -> 1 at rate eps and 1 -> 0 at rate 1 - eps, V moves 1 -> -1 at rate R(1+m)/2 and -1 -> 1 at rate R(1-m)/2, where eps = s^-2, R = s^4, alpha^2 = (1 - b^2 eps)/(1 - eps), m = b eps/(alpha(1 - eps)); g(y, v) = alpha(1 - y)v + b y. Then tau_2 = 1 (the spectrum of -Q is 0, 1, R, R+1), E_pi g = 0, E_pi g^2 = 1 and ||g||_inf = b. With H = {Y = 0 on [0, s]} and J = int_0^s V du: S_s = alpha J on H, P(H) = (1 - eps)e^{-eps s} >= 1 - eps(1+s), E_pi J = -ms and var_pi J <= 2(1 - m^2)s/R, so by Chebyshev P_pi(S_s <= 0) >= 1 - eps(1+s) - 2(1 - m^2)/(R m^2 s) >= 1 - 4/s. Hence at t = s the distance in Open Problem 4.30 is at least 1/2 - 4/s, also with sigma s^(1/2) replaced by any positive constant; s^2 sigma^2 -> 2b^2, and S_s/(sigma s^(1/2)) -> 0 in probability while its second moment tends to 1. Since ||g||_inf >= 1 for standardized g, no psi(b, .) -> 0 exists for any b. Positive side: Lezaud (2001), Theorem 3.1, gives the distance at most 26 b (tau_2/sigma^2)^(1/2) (t/tau_2)^(-1/2) + e^{-t/tau_2}, so the bound holds once sigma^2/tau_2 is bounded below.
statement_caveat: The source uses asymptotic variance normalization, permits arbitrary continuous transition rates, and starts in stationarity. The 13 Oct family covers every value b >= 1 of ||g||_infinity (the 6 Sep counterexample fixed ||g||_infinity = 2), and the bound P_pi(S_s <= 0) >= 1 - 4/s makes the conclusion independent of the normalization.

statement: If a consistent equivariant Borel flow rule has a stationary probability measure equivalent to Galton-Watson law, must the associated subtree Markov chain be ergodic?
title: Ergodicity of stationary Galton-Watson flows
result_status: ANSWERED: no, novelty not verified. Let GW have p2 = 3/5, p3 = 2/5. Colour generation n independently and uniformly and propagate upward, a vertex with two children taking the AND of their colours and a vertex with three children the OR; q_n = P(root colour 1 | first n generations) is a martingale, and the probability d_n that two independent colourings give the root different colours satisfies d_{n+1} = d_n(3 - d_n)^2/10 <= 9d_n/10 with d_0 = 1/2, so q_n -> C in {0, 1} a.s.: the colour C is a measurable, isomorphism-invariant function of the tree with P(C = 1) = 1/2 (the Johnson-Podder-Skerman interpretation of the fixed point 1/2, whose pivot tree has mean matrix diag(9/10, 9/10)). Every vertex has a child of its own colour. The flow rule spreads the flow uniformly over the children of the root that share its colour (on a full-measure Borel set; elsewhere over the infinite children). Then (i) GW is stationary; (ii) B = {C = 1} has GW(B) = 1/2 and p(T, B) = 1_B(T) a.s., so the chain from any stationary measure equivalent to GW, GW included, is not ergodic; (iii) GW(.|B) and GW(.|B^c) are stationary and ergodic, and the invariant sets are, up to null sets, the empty set, B, B^c and the whole space.
statement_caveat: The definition permits zero child weights; strict positivity is the separate sufficient hypothesis of Proposition 17.17, and Exercise 17.22 only treats a merely absolutely continuous stationary measure. The 13 Oct example gives zero flow to some child of the root with probability 3/5, as Proposition 17.17 forces any example to do with positive probability. Flow rules are taken equivariant, as the book assumes throughout, and stationarity and invariance are read on isomorphism-invariant events (the conventions of Chapter 17).

statement: Determine the limiting law of (D-E[D])/sqrt(Var(D)) for a typical LK(n,k) degree as the preference budget grows.
title: The standardized degree law in growing bilateral preference graphs
result_status: ANSWERED: the limit law is found in every regime, novelty not verified. Write D for the degree of a vertex of LK(n,k), H = k - D, s_n^2 = k(n-k)/n and g(z) = phi(z) + z Phi(z). (i) If k -> infinity and n - k -> infinity, H/s_n => g(Z) with Z standard normal, with convergence of the first two moments; so E D = k - s_n/sqrt(pi) + o(s_n), Var D = v s_n^2 + o(s_n^2) with v = 1/3 + (sqrt 3 - 2)/(2 pi), and (D - E D)/sqrt(Var D) => L_inf = (pi^(-1/2) - g(Z))/sqrt(v), a law with an explicit density whose values lie below 1.04643..., so not normal. (ii) If r = n - 1 - k >= 1 is fixed, H converges in law and in all moments to H_r, Poisson given A with mean Lambda_r(A) = e^(-A) sum_{l<r} (r - l) A^l/l!, A ~ Gamma(r,1); E H_r = mu_r = r C(2r,r)/4^r; the standardized limits L_r = (mu_r - H_r)/sqrt(nu_r) tend to L_inf as r -> infinity. (iii) If k is fixed, D converges in law and in all moments to the root degree of the Erlang weighted tree (Moharrami-Subramanian-Liu-Sundaresan, arXiv 2002.03993v5, Theorems 2.1 and 5.1: given the root threshold x, Binomial(k, 1 - q(x))), with a direct proof in the paper. (iv) Every subsequential limit of the standardized degree along any sequence k(n) is one of these; L_1 and L_2 differ (largest values sqrt(3/7) and sqrt(243/433)), so when n - 1 - k alternates between 1 and 2 there is no limit and no single law serves every sequence. (v) For every n and 1 <= k <= n - 2, E(k - D) is the same at the budgets k and n - 1 - k, equal to (n - 1) int_0^1 F(1 - F) dt with F the Beta(k, n - 1 - k) distribution function, which identifies the constant c_k = (2k - 1) C(2k - 2, k - 1)/2^(2k - 1) of the source's Theorem 7 as mu_k.
statement_caveat: D is the degree of a fixed vertex, which by symmetry has the law of the source's randomly chosen vertex. The standardized degree has no single limit over all sequences k(n); the answer identifies every subsequential limit. The fixed-k case is prior art (the Erlang weighted tree) and is cited, not claimed. The source lets a vertex choose the k edges with the largest scores and the paper the k smallest; the graph law is the same.

statement: Does a stationary ergodic CTMC on ordered intensity values exist that is not stochastically monotone but whose speed-scaled process decreases in supermodular stochastic order?
title: A nonmonotone Markov intensity with supermodular time ordering
result_status: ANSWERED YES, written up and posted: the star chain on the values 1 < 2 < 3 (from 1 it jumps to 2 at rate a2 and to 3 at rate a3, and returns to 1 from 2 at rate b2 and from 3 at rate b3) is stationary, ergodic and, for a2, a3 > 0, not stochastically monotone. (i) If b2 = b3 its speeded-up processes are nonincreasing in the supermodular order of processes for every finite set of sampling times, so the answer to Leskela's Problem 3 is yes. (ii) If b3 > b2 the order fails already for pairs: P(lambda(0) <= 1, lambda(t) <= 2) is strictly increasing for large t. (iii) For a reversible three-state chain with two distinct nonzero eigenvalues the pairs (lambda(0), lambda(t)) are ordered in t exactly when the slow left eigenvector l1 has l1(1) l1(3) <= 0; for the star chain this is b2 >= b3. The case b2 > b3 for more than two sampling times is left as a conjecture, supported by linear-programming tests. With values 0 <= v1 < v2 < v3 the result holds unchanged, and by Bauerle-Rolski 1998 the mean stationary workload of a stable single-server queue with Cox arrivals of intensity lambda_c is nonincreasing in c.
statement_caveat: This is an existence question about the stronger process order, distinct from workload ordering. The answer covers the star chains with b2 = b3 (all sampling times) and b3 > b2 (fails for pairs); the star chains with b2 > b3 are settled for pairs only.

statement: For two leaves separated by r_n positions in the cyclic interval representation, prove that their continuous-height correlation tends to1-alpha when log(r_n)/log(n) tends to alpha in[0,1].
title: Correlations of critical-tree leaves at mesoscopic separation
result_status: ANSWERED, written up and posted: rho(n, r_n) -> 1 - alpha for every alpha in [0,1]. Uniformly in 1 <= r <= n/2, Cov(D^(1), D^(2)) = sigma^2 log(n/r) + O(sqrt(log n)) and Var(D_n) = sigma^2 log n + O(sqrt(log n)) with sigma^2 = 2 zeta(3)/zeta(2)^3, so rho(n, r) = 1 - log r / log n + O((log n)^(-1/2)); for an oriented offset r the same holds with min(r, n - r). The proof uses the potential F(m, j) = log(j(m+1-j)/m) of a leaf at position j in a clade of m leaves, which decreases at rate zeta(2) with bracket rate 2 zeta(3) up to square-integrable errors, and compares the two leaves' martingales up to the cut that separates them; the covariance equals 2 zeta(3)/zeta(2)^2 times the mean time the two leaves share a clade, E S = log(n/r)/zeta(2) + O(1). Simulations (n = 2^20, 2^40) suggest O(1) errors, i.e. rate 1/log n, which is not proved.
statement_caveat: The macroscopic alpha=1 case is already established in the corrected published Aldous-Pittel result. All separation exponents form one question, not separate variants.

statement: Give a useful explicit joint stationary law for the ordered particles which drift at speed x and jump left at rate1 Poisson space-time points.
title: Explicit stationary law of the leftmost Hammersley drift-jump particles
result_status: ANSWERED: an explicit description of the stationary law, part of it known. (i) The k-particle process has a unique stationary law and the law at time t converges to it in total variation from every initial configuration (||mu_t - pi||_TV <= A e^(-t) + P_pi(X_k > A) for A < x_1 e^t). (ii) In stationarity (X_1, ..., X_k) = (Gamma_{tau_1}, ..., Gamma_{tau_k}) in law, Gamma_1 < Gamma_2 < ... a rate-one Poisson process and, independently, tau_i = min{n : ell_n >= i}, ell_n the longest increasing subsequence of n iid uniforms; equivalently P(X_{k_a} > s_a for all a) = P(L(s_a) <= k_a - 1 for all a), L the Poissonized longest increasing subsequence. This is equivalent to Aldous-Diaconis 1993 notes eq. (42), Gamma(B(i)), by the symmetry between pi and pi^(-1). (iii) For 0 < s_1 < ... < s_r = T and k_1 <= ... <= k_r, with d = k_r - 1, the probability is e^(-T) det [[A, F], [-G, -Q]] with A_ij = E_T(i,j), E_u(a,b) = u^((b-a)/2) I_{a-b}(2 sqrt u), F, G, Q built from p_u(a,b) = u^(a-b)/(a-b)! and E_u at the markers (s_a, z), 0 <= z <= d - k_a; size at most k(k-1) for the first k particles; for one particle Gessel's Toeplitz determinant e^(-T) det[I_{i-j}(2 sqrt T)]. (iv) E(X_i - X_{i-1}) = sum_n P(ell_n = i-1) = c(i) of Aldous-Diaconis 1999 Proposition 9, which answers the 1993 notes' p. 38 request for a direct reason; E X_2 = e.
statement_caveat: The representation (ii) is in the 1993 Aldous-Diaconis notes (eq. (42)) in the form Gamma(B(i)) and is credited there; the paper gives a self-contained proof with uniqueness and convergence and the identification of B with the LIS hitting times. The determinant (iii) is related to the Schur process / extended discrete Bessel kernel (Okounkov-Reshetikhin 2003, Borodin-Okounkov-Olshanski 2000), which gives Fredholm forms of the same probabilities; the finite form is not claimed as new beyond what was searched.

locator: Problem 7.5, p. 125 of Probab. Theory Related Fields 160 (2014); PDF page 26 of arXiv:1302.6958v4
result_status: ANSWERED: yes, and absolute continuity suffices. If the law of (X_t, t >= 0) is absolutely continuous with respect to Wiener measure then, on an extension of the probability space, there are a standard Brownian motion B and an a.s. finite random integer N >= 0 with X_t = B_{N+t} - B_N for all t >= 0; N cannot in general be a stopping time for B. General form: for an invertible measure-preserving theta of (E, P) and a density f, a randomized forward shift theta^N (N built from a P-distributed point and independent uniforms) carries P to fP iff E[f | I] = 1, I the invariant sigma-field; deterministic shift rules reach only integer-valued densities; E N can be infinite.
